claims.quote: The Exeter incident or Incident at Exeter was a highly publicized UFO sighting that occurred on September 3, 1965, approximately 3 miles (5 km) south of Exeter, New Hampshire, in the neighboring town of Kensington.

claims.v: approximately 2:00 a.m.
claims.quote: On September 3, 1965, at approximately 2:00 a.m., 18-year-old Norman Muscarello was hitchhiking to his home in Exeter along New Hampshire Route 150.

claims.v: United States
claims.quote: The Exeter incident or Incident at Exeter was a highly publicized UFO sighting that occurred on September 3, 1965, approximately 3 miles (5 km) south of Exeter, New Hampshire, in the neighboring town of Kensington.

Although several separate sightings had been reported in the Exeter area by numerous witnesses in the weeks leading up to the specific incident, it was the September 3 sighting, involving a local teenager and two police officers which became, by far, the most famous.

claims.v: approximately 3 miles (5 km) south

claims.v: highly publicized
claims.quote: The Exeter incident or Incident at Exeter was a highly publicized UFO sighting that occurred on September 3, 1965, approximately 3 miles (5 km) south of Exeter, New Hampshire, in the neighboring town of Kensington.

claims.v: received national publicity
claims.quote: The sightings by Muscarello and the two policemen received national publicity.

claims.v: several separate sightings reported in the Exeter area by numerous witnesses in the preceding weeks
claims.quote: Although several separate sightings had been reported in the Exeter area by numerous witnesses in the weeks leading up to the specific incident, it was the September 3 sighting, involving a local teenager and two police officers which became, by far, the most famous.

claims.v: among the best-documented and best-publicized in UFO history
claims.quote: The Exeter UFO sightings—and particularly the September 3 sightings involving Norman Muscarello and police officers Eugene Bertrand and David Hunt—remain among the best-documented and best-publicized in UFO history.

claims.v: Air Force unable to identify the object
claims.quote: Spaulding wrote that "based on additional information submitted to our UFO investigation officer, Wright-Patterson AFB, Ohio, we have been unable to identify the object you observed on September 3, 1965."

claims.v: little traffic on the highway at that hour of the morning
claims.quote: Since he had recently sold his car, Muscarello would hitchhike to and from Amesbury; however, at that hour of the morning there was little traffic on the highway, and Muscarello had walked a good part of the distance.

claims.v: weather clear, no wind, no chance of weather inversion (per the policemen)
claims.quote: and went to considerable trouble to confirm that the weather was clear, there was no wind, no chance of weather inversion, and that what we were seeing was in no way a military or civilian aircraft.

claims.v: a couple in an approaching car drove Muscarello to the Exeter police station
claims.quote: The couple in the car drove the frightened youth to the Exeter police station.

claims.v: a frightened woman told Bertrand a huge object with flashing red lights had followed her car from Epping to Exeter and hovered over it
claims.quote: When Bertrand stopped to ask if she had a problem, the woman told him that a "huge object with flashing red lights" had followed her car from Epping to Exeter, a distance of about 12 miles (19 km) and hovered over the car before flying away.

claims.v: Exeter's police chief called Pease Air Force Base and reported a UFO sighting
claims.quote: After Exeter's police chief read the reports of Muscarello, Bertrand, Hunt, he called nearby Pease Air Force Base and reported a UFO sighting.

claims.v: Air Force officers asked the three witnesses not to report their sighting to the press
claims.quote: The Air Force officers asked all three not to report their sighting to the press, but a reporter from the Manchester Union-Leader newspaper had already interviewed them.

claims.v: the policemen said they were the subject of considerable ridicule after the Pentagon evaluation
claims.quote: The two policemen sent a letter to Project Blue Book in which they stated, "As you can imagine, we have been the subject of considerable ridicule since the Pentagon released its 'final evaluation' of our sighting of September 3, 1965

claims.v: an Air Force officer had Pease AFB lights activated before a large crowd to prove the UFOs were base lights; nothing was seen
claims.quote: According to Fowler, "he ordered personnel at the base to turn the lights on. Everybody looked and waited—and nothing happened. Frustrated, he yelled into the mic to turn on the lights. A voice replied that the lights were on.

claims.v: the embarrassed officer drove off amid the laughs and jeers of the crowd
claims.quote: The very embarrassed officer slunk back into the seat of the staff car and drove off amongst the laughs and jeers of the crowd.

claims.v: sighting took place nearly an hour after Operation Big Blast was said to have ended
